clue.text: Cut grass concealing I am rustic

indicators.note: the grass word hides the rustic phrase inside itself, wrapping round it

parts.note: rye is a cereal grass
'I be' is the dialect, countrified form of 'I am'

explanation.surface: A country type speaks while hiding in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am rustic' is the rural dialect 'I be', which goes inside RYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib-eye is a cut of beef steak taken from the rib section.

clue.text: "Thus?" is a poor question!

indicators.note: a poor version of the word is a badly formed one, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a one-word query is not a well-framed question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thus?' stands for a word put in quotation marks, as when a writer flags a so-called term; the anagram of QUESTION gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: A word written in quotation marks is flagged as cited exactly so, the way 'thus' or sic marks a quoted form.

clue.text: Beat bandleader having new venue for such fare

indicators.note: beaten material is pounded out of shape, so these letters are reworked
a new version of the word venue is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: A bandleader is beaten up for choosing a different venue for the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' and 'new' both signal the shuffle: BANDLEADER and VENUE together rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread baked without yeast is eaten at Passover, so it is a kind of food or fare.

clue.text: Couple at the races continually improving

definitions.meaning: two punters placing wagers at a racecourse, one gambler and another
getting steadily more good all the time

explanation.definitionFit: Two gamblers are a pair of punters joined by 'and', while the phrase also means progressing ever upward in quality.

clue.text: One of 20, maybe, is a reasonable advantage

definitions.meaning: 20 across is a suit of playing cards, so a single card of that suit is held in a player's grip
a margin kept in reserve, a comfortable lead

explanation.definitionFit: A playing card of the 20-across suit is held by the player, and a reserve margin gives a comfortable lead.

clue.text: Get angry with date on top of article

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to date someone is to see them romantically
'the' is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone fumes about a date being put ahead of an article.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil with inward fury, a synonym for getting angry.

clue.text: Direct through the exit, OK?

parts.note: having gone out of the door
'right?' is a way of asking 'all right, okay?'

explanation.surface: A doorman points someone straight through the exit and asks if that is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright refusal is direct and unqualified, so both words mean straightforward.

clue.text: Small and dainty female fighter has new love around

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

indicators.note: the love word wraps round the letter for new, enclosing it

parts.note: love means nothing or zero in tennis, so none

explanation.surface: A woman pilot of a fighter plane has a new romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The French feminine form is the one used of a woman, hence 'female' within the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the feminine adjective describes a petite, delicately pretty woman.

clue.text: Press broken by writer to begin the firing

indicators.note: the press abbreviation is split apart with the writer placed in the gap

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press
a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: A printing press is wrecked by a writer before a shooting begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to start shooting, as guns open up on a target.

clue.text: Dry start to summer announced by stammerer

indicators.note: a stammerer saying the word repeats its opening sound, so the month comes out with a stutter

parts.note: the first month of the summer season

explanation.surface: Someone with a stammer stumbles over naming the first summer month.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuttering the month gives 'Je-June', which is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune prose is dull and uninteresting, dry in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Glitterati find their luck here

definitions.meaning: the heavens where astrologers read people's fortunes

explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities are famous names, and horoscopes read fortune in the heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Reviewed U2 guitarist's Cracked Up

parts.note: to go over something is to review it
The Edge is the lead guitarist of the Irish band U2

explanation.surface: A critic reviewed a U2 guitarist's album called Cracked Up.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over the edge is losing one's sanity, an idiom for cracking up.

clue.text: A ditty written about unnamed deserter, one who is out of favour?

definitions.text: one who is out of favour?

parts.note: 'a' as in 'ten pounds a head' means per

indicators.note: the ditty is written round the unnamed word, enclosing it

parts.note: a ditty is a simple song
anon is short for anonymous
a rat deserts a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Someone composes a little song about an anonymous turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names an unwelcome individual, typically a diplomat expelled by a host country.

clue.text: Aroma heard to contend with brandy

indicators.note: the smell word is spoken, giving a French-looking spelling of the same sound

parts.note: an aroma is a smell or odour
to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: Smells and competing sensations mingle as someone sips brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means water of life and names a clear fruit brandy.

clue.text: New plans for revolutionary water transport

parts.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary
rafts are simple boats carrying people over water

explanation.surface: A revolutionary has fresh schemes for boats on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Redrafts are revised versions of documents, fresh plans drawn up again.

clue.text: Saw nothing "untoward" nurse's routine" rounds?

indicators.note: the whole string is turned round so it reads from the far end

parts.note: to have eyed something is to have seen it
nil means nothing
untoward means bad or improper
EN is an enrolled nurse
a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A nurse doing ward rounds sees nothing amiss in the routine, deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray quotation marks are print noise. 'rounds' turns the whole run EYED NIL BAD EN RUT backwards, and the whole clue also describes a nurse ignoring misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately ignoring wrongdoing is seeing nothing improper, as a complicit nurse might.

clue.text: Hold originator of famous pecking order?

definitions.meaning: a wrestling grip around the neck from behind
the admiral whose dying request 'Kiss me, Hardy' asked for a peck

explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling neck lock carries the admiral's name, and his dying words asked his captain for a kiss.

clue.text: Elementary Tees anagrams I cry about

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the two tees
the word openly tells the solver to rearrange the following letters

parts.note: the letter T twice, two tees

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over anagrams made from the River Tees.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is the North-East English river, but here it is two letter Ts, held inside the rearranged I CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttric means relating to yttrium, a chemical element, hence elementary.

clue.text: The Spanish version of Earl's Court accommodating wine store

indicators.note: the court abbreviation houses the other letters within it

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'

indicators.note: a version of the title is a rearranged form of its letters

parts.note: the noble title, its possessive ignored

explanation.surface: An Earl's Court in Spain has room for a wine cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl's Court is a district of London, but here 'Earl's' is shuffled to LARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a cabinet or sideboard for keeping bottles.

clue.text: One near midfield in county football club

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the county close to its middle

parts.note: Herts is the abbreviation for Hertfordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A player stands close to the centre of the pitch for a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: HERTS is Hertfordshire, a county north of London; Hearts is the Edinburgh club Heart of Midlothian.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is the nickname of Heart of Midlothian, a Scottish football club.

clue.text: Aims high to pot flash plant

indicators.note: potting something holds it inside, so the shuffled letters contain the flash
someone high is intoxicated and the letters reel about

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: A gardener aims high to put a showy plant into a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering shrub of the acacia family, so a plant.

clue.text: A mug from abroad becomes a genius

parts.note: ein is German for 'a'
a stein is a German beer mug

explanation.surface: A tankard bought overseas turns out to be brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's surname is used generically for anyone of brilliant intellect.
